title: Machine installation
text: Keep the machine connected while backing up its universe and completing cleanup that needs the server. Then remove the connection or finish uninstalling and save the reported machine ID. For each server that remains available, the owner or a server administrator can run `yoke --env ENV machine retire MACHINE_ID --confirm` from another machine connected to it. Retirement revokes the machine credential. Machine uninstall on macOS, systemd Linux and Windows removes saved relay services (launchd jobs, systemd units, scheduled tasks) even after their connection aliases were removed, and on Windows waits up to 30 seconds for each relay's processes to exit, failing with `uninstall_relay_not_stopped` and the PID when one stays running. It first requests graceful browser shutdown, stops Browser QA daemons and kills processes still running from Yoke's Playwright cache after 10 seconds. It reports stopped processes by name and PID and refuses before the relay or any other removal step if a process in the cache survives. Uninstall removes the temporary handoff folder after cancelling the worker or when Windows denies breakaway. If the detached CLI removal fails, its log names a shell command that removes the releases folder without yoke. On Windows the worker breaks away from the session's job so it survives an SSH session closing; a job that forbids breakaway fails the CLI handoff with `uninstall_cli_handoff_failed`, keeps the CLI and machine home, and names that command. Unproven ownership or a failed stop retains the machine home and CLI for recovery.
